body:
WHAT
Bash runs a shell command through Git Bash (or bash on POSIX), merges stdout and stderr into one result, and kills the whole process tree if the command exceeds its timeout (default 120s, max 600s). Before running, a deletion matcher decides if the command is destructive so the permission engine can ask the user: ten single words (rm, del, rimraf, ...) and twelve phrases (git clean, drop table, ...) are matched case-insensitively as whole tokens, plus three special patterns (git branch -D case-sensitive, git checkout -- <path>, find ... -delete) and a mv rule (destructive only with -f/--force or a destination outside the workspace).

WHY
Without whole-token matching, harmless commands like 'npm run del-lint' or 'format' would trigger deletion prompts; without the special cases, real deletions like 'git branch -D' would slip through; without tree kill, a timed-out command would leave orphan children running.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/bash.ts — DELETION_SINGLE_WORDS, DELETION_PHRASES, DELETION_PATTERN, GIT_BRANCH_FORCE_DELETE, GIT_CHECKOUT_DISCARD, FIND_DELETE, MV_SEGMENT, mvIsDestructive(), bashDeletionSubject() (exported), bashDeletionScope()/bashDeletionTargets() (workspace/unknown/protected classification), bashTool (permissionClass 'execute', deletionSubject, foreground-sleep block), runForeground() (timeout branch calls killTree() and returns 'Command timed out after ...', clip() to 30k chars, non-zero exit sets isError), spawnShell(), killTree() (taskkill /T /F on win32, process.kill(-pid) elsewhere), resolveBashPath().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. bashDeletionSubject returns the command for 'rm -rf build', 'RM x', 'echo a && del b', 'git clean -fd', 'DROP TABLE users', 'kubectl delete pod x' and 'trash foo' (whole tokens, case-insensitive, after separators).
2. bashDeletionSubject returns undefined for 'npm run del-lint', 'format', 'mkdir x', 'git branch -d old', 'mv a b', 'git checkout main' and 'find . -name x' (no false positive on substrings or safe forms).
3. bashDeletionSubject returns the command for the three special-cased shapes and the mv rule: 'git branch -D old' (while 'git branch -d old' stays undefined — case-sensitive), 'git checkout -- src/a.ts' (while 'git checkout --' with no path stays undefined), 'find . -name "*.tmp" -delete', 'mv -f a b', 'mv a /tmp/b' and 'mv a ../b'.
4. Execute Bash { command: 'echo out; echo err 1>&2; exit 2', description } in a temp cwd; assert content contains both 'out' and 'err' and isError is true; with 'exit 0' and no output, content is '(no output)'.
5. Execute Bash { command: 'sleep 30', timeout: 500 } (note: a bare 'sleep N' is blocked, so use 'sleep 30; echo x' or a subshell); assert it resolves in about 500ms with isError:true, content starting 'Command timed out after 500ms', and the child pid is no longer alive afterwards.
